findings.defect: The lemma is false as stated: it says "a rooted binary tree of $r-1$ Max vertices" and then sets $d:=\lceil\log_2 r\rceil$, but the induction in the proof is an induction on the TREE HEIGHT, so the tree must be balanced; an unbalanced binary tree with $r$ leaves has height up to $r-1$ and the root then lags by $r-1$ rounds.
findings.evidence: Explicit counterexample, exact arithmetic (/tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/paper-audit-laws/maxtree.py): the one-player stopping SSG on 11 vertices with Vmax={p,q,r}, p->(q,A4), q->(r,A3), r->(t1,A2), gadgets A2,A3,A4 of constant values 1/8, 1/4, 1/2 and the action r->t1 of value 1, started at p|->A4, q|->A3, r|->A2. r=4 actions, all four action values constant throughout, d=ceil(log2 4)=2. The all-switches run is {r},{q},{p}: after round 0 p=1/2 q=1/4 r=1/8; after round 1 p=1/2 q=1/4 r=1; after round 2 p=1/2 q=1 r=1 -- the root still holds 1/2, not the maximum 1; it reaches 1 only after 3 rounds. The proof's first sentence, "a vertex at height one compares its two leaves", is exactly where balance is assumed. One-word repair: "balanced rooted binary tree ... of height d".

findings.defect: The section introduction claims the class $\mathcal K_1$ contains "an explicit family in it that none of \Cref{sec:special}'s theorems reaches". That is false: $K_n$ carries an escape certificate of def:survival with $\lambda$ and $\kappa(x)$ both constant in $n$, so thm:escape-class (l.1617, inside sec:special) decides prob:main on the family in polynomial time.
findings.evidence: Exact certificate, verified for n = 1,2,3,5,8,12,20,40 (escape.py): lambda = 19/20 and x(x_i)=3, x(m_i)=60/19, x(c_i)=1000/361, x(d_i)=40/19, x(e_i)=1 for every block i. Then x >= 1 and Sx <= lambda*x with equality at m_i, c_i, d_i: Sx(e_i)=0; Sx(d_i)=(1+3)/2=2=(19/20)(40/19); Sx(m_i)=max(3,40/19)=3=(19/20)(60/19); Sx(c_i)=(60/19+40/19)/2=50/19=(19/20)(1000/361); Sx(x_i)=max(1000/361,1)=2.770...<=(19/20)*3=2.85. kappa(x)=60/19=3.157..., log2(1/lambda)=0.0740, both independent of n, so thm:escape-class's hypothesis (log2 kappa = poly(N), log2(1/lambda) >= 1/poly(N)) holds and its bound is O(N + (a+log2 kappa)/log2(1/lambda)) = O(N) iterations of T. Independently, lem:escape-rate gives lambda*(K_n) = 2^{-1/3} for every n, since the only cycle of K_n is x_i->c_i->m_i->x_i of weight 1/2 over three steps.

findings.defect: "$\mathcal K_1$ escapes the four combinatorial classes of \Cref{sec:special}" is stale: sec:special (l.1223-3190) now proves eight polynomial-class theorems, and prop:k1-family addresses only thm:avg-acyclic, thm:player-free, thm:one-player and thm:few-avg.
findings.evidence: Unaddressed classes in sec:special: thm:few-escape (l.1480), thm:escape-class (l.1617), thm:kacyclic (l.2255), thm:few-denominator (l.2617), thm:modulator (l.3012), thm:qp (l.3073). Of these, thm:escape-class does reach K_n (see the major finding). thm:kacyclic does not apply -- I enumerated all cycles of K_n for n<=4 and every cycle is x_i->c_i->m_i->x_i, carrying all three kinds -- but the proposition never says so. Contrast prop:modulator-family (l.3155), which compares against six. The same undercount is repeated at l.372 and l.13469 ("the four preceding it").

findings.defect: "no such perturbation makes $B'$ of \Cref{prop:overshoot-small} nondegenerate, all ten of its ties being ties at $0$": $B'$ has 26 ties, not ten; ten is the tie count of the DAMPED game $G'=B'_7$, which prop:overshoot-small carefully distinguishes from $B'$.
findings.evidence: Exact recomputation (ties.py). B' (12 non-sink vertices, not stopping, val_sigma taken as the least fixed point) has 26 tied incidences (sigma,i) out of 64: 10 at value 0, 11 at 3/4 and 5 at 1. B'_7 has exactly 10 ties, all at 0, listed as ((0,1,0,0),2), ((0,1,1,0),2), ((1,0,0,0),1), ((1,0,0,0),2), ((1,0,1,0),1), ((1,0,1,0),2), ((1,1,0,0),1), ((1,1,0,0),2), ((1,1,1,0),1), ((1,1,1,0),2). The 16 ties of B' at 3/4 and 1 are exactly the ones damping removes, so the sentence's count contradicts its own point.

findings.defect: "on an acyclic orientation it terminates" is asserted inside a definition and never proved anywhere in the manuscript; prop:auso-size (l.4655) asserts the same ("A bottom-antipodal trace of an acyclic orientation visits distinct vertices") with no proof, and prop:auso-census (l.4903) confirms it only exhaustively for m<=4. The ceilings h*(m), cor:ceiling-general and cor:f-auso all rest on it.
findings.evidence: The claim is true and has a two-line proof, which the manuscript should carry: in the face F spanned by u and u+s(u), s_F(x):=s(x)∩J is an AUSO with source u; its coordinatewise complement is again a unique sink orientation (the condition (s(x)+s(y))∩(x+y)≠0 is invariant under complementing s) and is acyclic (edge reversal of an acyclic digraph), so from every vertex of F its unique sink -- which is u -- is reachable; reversing that path gives an s-path from u to u+s(u), whence u < u+s(u) strictly in the acyclic reachability order and the walk cannot repeat a vertex. I verified the statement exhaustively at m=2 and m=3 (12 and 728 AUSOs, 0 BA cycles; antipode reachable in every case, including the 16 cyclic USOs of the 3-cube).

findings.defect: The closed form $w^\ast(x_1)=\tfrac12+2^{-(n+1)}$ and "a bound attained" are quantified over all $n\ge1$ but justified only as "exact computations", with no $n$ named -- an infinite family's value proved by finitely many evaluations.
findings.evidence: I verified stopping, N=5n+2, a=3n, |Vmax|=|Vmin|=n, singleton H-components, w*(x_1)=1/2+2^{-(n+1)} and max run length exactly n over all 2^n starts, for n=1..7 (k1.py). The value formula has a three-line proof the manuscript omits: with E_i=1/2, D_i=(E_i+V_{i+1})/2, M_i=min(V_i,D_i), C_i=(M_i+D_i)/2, V_i=max(C_i,E_i) and V_{n+1}=1, the vector V_i=D_i=M_i=C_i=1/2+2^{-(n-i+2)}, E_i=1/2 is a fixed point of T, unique because K_n is stopping. GAP (missing statement, one sentence): "for every n>=1 some initial Max strategy of K_n makes the all-switches run take exactly n rounds" -- measured here only for n<=7.

findings.defect: "\Cref{def:damping} makes such a tree cheap" cites the wrong result: def:damping is the chain of average vertices that damps an edge, and it says nothing about the cost of a tree of Max vertices; lem:max-tree, the result that does, prices the tree at $r-1$ Max vertices and explicitly "no average vertex".
findings.evidence: def:damping (l.951) replaces each edge by m average vertices delivering the head with probability 1-2^{-m}; lem:max-tree (l.3879) states "the cost is $r-1$ Max vertices and no average vertex". The two are unrelated, and l.3903 says the binarisation is "the standard out-degree-two normalisation, which \Cref{rem:closed-now-or-never} already used in prose" -- so the forward reference is to a claim that cites the wrong lemma.

findings.defect: The instance cannot be reconstructed from the text and its numbers read as contradictory: "a three-vertex lane with exits worth $\tfrac78,\tfrac34,\tfrac58$" followed by "the best leaf is worth $1$". The lane vertices, not the exits, are the leaves, and the lemma's hypothesis (leaf values constant) is exactly what fails here -- the third lane vertex has an unmentioned action to $t_1$, of value 1.
findings.evidence: I rebuilt the instance exactly (lane.py): 15 vertices, 5 Max (l1,l2,l3,u,p), 8 average, stopping, with l1->(l2, 7/8), l2->(l3, 3/4), l3->(t1, 5/8), u->(l1,l2), p->(u,l3). From the start "all three lane vertices exit, u|->l1, p|->u" the all-switches run is {l3},{l2,p},{l1,u}, three rounds; at t=0 best leaf 7/8 = root 7/8, at t=1 best leaf 1 and root 7/8. So the numbers are right but only for t=1 and only once l3->t1 is disclosed. Also "at the first round" should say after the first round.

findings.defect: "it holds along the ladder $L_n$ of \Cref{def:ladder}, whose run has length $2^{n}-1$": the paragraph is about all-switches runs, and the all-switches run on $L_n$ has length $n$; $2^n-1$ is the least-index / smallest-gap run of thm:ladder, which the citation does not name.
findings.evidence: def:ladder (l.6766) defines L_n only; thm:ladder (l.6777) proves 2^n-1 for the least-index rule, and rem:ladder/l.6848 records "The all-switches rule terminates on L_n in exactly n rounds". The preceding two sentences of rem:impedance read "Along an all-switches run let u be at rest at sigma_t...", so the reader carries the all-switches reading into the ladder sentence.

findings.defect: "A delay of $d$ rounds is likewise cheap, a chain of $d$ Max vertices whose second actions are constants" is stated without the caveat that such a chain fires once: a Max vertex whose two options are a variable and a constant switches at most twice along any improving run, so the chain cannot re-arm, which is precisely the reusability the GAP two sentences later needs.
findings.evidence: Along an improving run val_sigma is nondecreasing, so for a Max vertex v with options (X, K) with K constant: if it points at K it switches to X the first time val(X) > K and never returns; if it starts at X it can switch to K once and back once. At most two switches. This is the manuscript's own standing observation (rem:bsi-br's round-15 rbr audit, cited in the round briefing). The published counters the paragraph is trying to transcribe re-arm their delays in every iteration.

findings.defect: $P$ is used with two incompatible meanings and the uniqueness argument is stated for the wrong matrix: "the substochastic matrix obtained from $P$ by deleting row and column $u$" has spectral radius 1 if $P$ is "the transition matrix of $M_{\sigma,\tau}$" as the setup says, because the absorbing sink rows survive the deletion.
findings.evidence: The first-step system "$h(x\to u)=\sum_w P(x,w)h(w\to u)$ with $h(\mathrm{sink}\to u)=0$" needs sinks as columns of P; the later display "$f=Pf+\beta$ ... $\mathcal N'=(I-P')^{-1}$" needs P restricted to the non-sinks. The rows of t_0 and t_1 must be deleted along with row and column u for the spectral-radius claim. Purely a wording defect: the theorem itself is correct -- verified on 2823 (game, profile, switched vertex) instances over random stopping games with 3 to 8 non-sinks, all three kinds present and sinks allowed as successors, 0 mismatches, and h=h' in every case (imped.py).

findings.defect: "The theorem writes that round's rise at $u$ as $(\val_{\sigma_{t'}}(b)-\val_{\sigma_{t'}}(a))/(1-h)$" overstates thm:impedance, which computes the change in $v_{\sigma,\tau}$ for a SINGLE switch in a FIXED positional pair; an all-switches round moves every vertex of $S_{t'}$ at once and Min re-optimises, so the theorem does not compute that round's rise.
findings.evidence: thm:impedance's hypothesis is "$(\sigma,\tau)$ a positional pair ... and let $P'$ be the chain obtained by switching $u$ from $a$ to $b$" -- one coordinate of one pair. The gap decomposition invoked next, cor:selfread, is moreover stated only for one-player games (l.3604). The paragraph's conclusion (lem:rise-bound applied to sigma_t and sigma_{t'+1}) is correct and is what carries the point; the sentence about "that round's rise" should be restricted to a single switch with Min frozen.

findings.defect: "an exponential all-switches run needs $\Omega(\log)$ many Max vertices pairwise mutually reachable" -- $\Omega(\log)$ of what is not said, and the bound actually forces $\Omega(N)$ for an exponential run; $\Omega(\log N)$ is what a superpolynomial run forces.
findings.evidence: thm:component-bound gives L <= sum_j (2^{|C_j|}-1) <= m*2^k with k the largest component size, so L = 2^{cN} forces k >= cN - log2 m, and L superpolynomial in N forces k = omega(log N). Verified empirically on 400 random stopping games (comp.py): no run exceeded sum_j(2^{|C_j|}-1) nor |Vmax|(2^k-1)/k.

findings.defect: "The published exponential lower bounds for locally-optimising strategy improvement --- on parity games, and for Howard's rule on Markov decision processes ---" are described with no attribution; Friedmann is nowhere cited in the manuscript and Christ-Yannakakis is not cited either.
findings.evidence: grep over frontier.tex: "Friedmann" has 0 hits, "Christ" 0 hits; "Fearnley" appears at l.2976, l.3128 and l.3909, the last for a different purpose (the binarisation GAP). The manuscript's own standard is that rediscovered or invoked prior art is named; the round briefing names Friedmann 2011 (parity/mean-payoff/discounted/SSG), Fearnley 2010 (total- and average-reward MDPs) and Christ-Yannakakis 2023 (reachability MDPs) as exactly these results.

findings.defect: Three "verified on K instances" claims do not say what was varied: "544 (game, profile, switched vertex) instances over stopping games", "714 run pairs of 250 random two-player stopping games", "671 run pairs of 250 random two-player stopping games". Only rem:impedance's SECOND run states the variation (three to eight non-sinks, all three kinds, sinks allowed as successors).
findings.evidence: My independent runs, with the variation stated: thm:impedance on 2823 (game, profile, switched vertex) instances over random stopping games with 3-8 non-sinks, all three kinds, sinks allowed as successors, 0 mismatches and h=h' throughout; cor:selfread on 2019 one-player instances of the same shape, 0 failures; thm:peak-law/cor:peak-sharp/cor:no-return/cor:law-b/cor:antichain on 1070 all-switches runs and 689 run pairs from ~250 random two-player stopping games with 4-8 non-sinks and all three kinds, 0 failures; lem:rise-bound on 1451 (run pair, at-rest Max vertex) instances of the same games, 0 failures; lem:monotone-law on 2383 strategy pairs, 0 failures (laws.py).

findings.defect: "The three laws are genuine constraints" but $f(m)$ is defined from two of them only (cor:no-return and cor:law-b); cor:antichain is a consequence of cor:no-return, so it contributes nothing to $f$, and the sentence invites the reader to think three laws were imposed.
findings.evidence: cor:antichain's own proof (l.4070-4076) derives it from cor:no-return at t'=t+2. My exhaustive search imposing exactly cor:no-return and cor:law-b reproduces f(m)=1,2,4,7,13 for m=1..5, and the length profile 31, 750, 12390, 135930, 967560, 4378320, 12280440, 20388600, 19136400, 9748080, 2550240, 347640, 22320 at m=5, matching prop:hstar-five's list exactly (f5.c).

findings.defect: "\Cref{cor:f-auso} settles that: every bottom-antipodal trace of an acyclic unique sink orientation obeys both laws" attributes to cor:f-auso a statement that is lem:auso-laws'; and "which is known to be exponential" carries no reference where rem:f-auso supplies one.
findings.evidence: cor:f-auso (l.4593) states only $f(m)\ge h^\ast(m)$; lem:auso-laws (l.4348) is "Every bottom-antipodal trace obeys the two laws". rem:f-auso (l.4613-4620) attributes the exponential growth of $h^\ast$ to Schurr and Szabo and to thm:blowup; rem:allsw-laws cites neither.

findings.defect: The 253-vertex nondegenerate realisation of $B'$'s run is neither printed in the paper nor committed under /data/ssg-proof/scripts, unlike every other explicit instance in this range; it rests entirely on "the round-15 verification route" and "its auditor".
findings.evidence: No file in /data/ssg-proof/scripts/round15-verify or /data/ssg-proof/scripts/blowup contains it (grep for 253 over frontier.tex returns only l.4240; over scripts/, nothing). The claim is however sound: I found an equivalent instance in 3 random tries (realise253b.py) -- B' re-damped with each edge leaking 2^{-7} to t_0 and a per-edge 2^{-j} to t_1 -- nondegenerate (0 ties over all 64 incidences), improvement outmap (12,11,14,13,0,15,10,9,4,3,2,1,8,5,7,6), a Holt-Klee AUSO of height 6, one of exactly six AUSO completions of s_{B'_7} whose bottom-antipodal walk from the start reproduces the run {0,3},{0,1,2},{0,1},{1},{2},{3}. So "its orientation class" is not single-valued: s_{B'_7} is not itself a unique sink orientation (7 violating pairs), and there are 24 AUSO completions of it, 6 of them run-matching (all Holt-Klee of height 6).

findings.defect: "The all-switches rule is the one rule for which a polynomial bound would immediately settle \Cref{prob:main}, since each of its rounds is one Min best response and one evaluation" -- the justification applies to every rule with a polynomial-time round, not only to all-switches.
findings.evidence: thm:gap-equivalence ((Poly-Rule)) states that a switching rule halting in polynomially many rounds from every start exists iff SSG-Value is in P; and the manuscript's own R_BR (prop:bsi-br) and the least-index rule also have polynomial rounds. "the one rule" should be "the canonical rule" or similar.

findings.defect: "any argument that bounds the number of iterations by (range of a potential)/(minimum increment) is inherently exponential --- independently of which potential is chosen" is not what thm:impedance gives: the theorem bounds only the change in the VALUE vector, so it constrains potentials whose increment is the value gain, and says nothing about a potential unrelated to the value.
findings.evidence: The general statement is cor:no-height's (l.6949: no progress measure of polynomial height on the Max strategy lattice), and the manuscript's own remark at l.6969 draws exactly that line -- "\Cref{thm:impedance} rules out potentials of polynomial range" -- without the "independently of which potential is chosen" clause.

findings.defect: Two small omissions: cor:isolated says "for every $t'>t$" where the run is only defined up to $L$ (read $t<t'\le L$); and cor:selfread's proof uses, without saying so, that $r(b)=h$, i.e. that "reaches $p$ strictly before $t_1$" and "ever visits $p$" coincide.
findings.evidence: lem:excursion (l.465) defines r(u) as Pr_u[v reached strictly before t_1]; the identification with Pr_b[ever visit p] holds because t_1 is absorbing, and it is what turns lem:excursion's q(b)+r(b)val(p) into the corollary's h*val(a)+(1-h)*ell with ell = q(b)/(1-h). cor:selfread itself is correct: verified on 2019 one-player instances over random stopping games with 3-8 non-sinks (display, the strict-switchability iff, and val_{sigma[p]}(p)=ell), 0 failures.

findings.defect: Possible unattributed prior art: the lemma is the classical policy-improvement comparison statement (if no vertex of the difference set is strictly switchable then the other strategy is no better), standard since Howard; the manuscript proves it from scratch with no remark that it is standard, where lem:sw a few pages later is properly attributed to Szabo and Welzl.
findings.evidence: From memory, unchecked against a source. Low confidence -- the statement in this exact contrapositive form, over an arbitrary difference set and with rem:monotone-law-general's stopping-free extension via thm:lfp-general(a)'s minimality clause, may well be the manuscript's own packaging. Flagged only because the manuscript's stated standard is that a rediscovery presented as new is a defect.
